Title: Load completeness
User Story: As a data analyst, I want every source order to be loaded or rejected, so that no data silently disappears.
Acceptance Criteria: Source order count = loaded + rejected; customer counts match.

Title: Order uniqueness
User Story: As a finance user, I want each order loaded once, so that revenue is not overstated.
Acceptance Criteria: No order_id appears more than once in fact_orders; duplicates are rejected.

Title: Mandatory fields and valid customers
User Story: As a data analyst, I want every loaded order to belong to a known customer, so that customer reports are complete.
Acceptance Criteria: customer_id is never null; every loaded order matches a row in dim_customers.

Title: Business rules
User Story: As a finance user, I want invalid quantities and prices rejected, so that totals are trustworthy.
Acceptance Criteria: Quantity >= 1 and unit_price >= 0 are accepted; quantity <= 0 and negative prices are rejected.

Title: Calculation accuracy
User Story: As a finance user, I want order_total to equal quantity x unit_price, so that revenue figures are correct.
Acceptance Criteria: order_total differs from quantity x unit_price by no more than 0.005 for every row.

Title: Date validity
User Story: As a reporting user, I want only valid calendar dates loaded, so that time-based reports work.
Acceptance Criteria: Loaded dates are valid; leap-day rules respected; invalid dates are rejected.

Title: Country standardization
User Story: As an analyst, I want consistent country names, so that grouping by country is accurate.
Acceptance Criteria: Only India, USA, UK, Germany or Unknown appear in dim_customers.

Title: Exception handling
User Story: As a data steward, I want every rejected row to carry a reason, so that data issues can be traced and fixed.
Acceptance Criteria: Every rejected row has a non-empty reject_reason; known bad records are all caught.

Title: Pipeline robustness
User Story: As an engineer, I want the ETL to handle empty input and re-runs safely, so that scheduled jobs do not corrupt data.
Acceptance Criteria: Empty source loads nothing without failing; re-running does not double the row counts.

Title: API data access
User Story: As an application developer, I want a read-only API for orders and customers, so that I can consume clean data.
Acceptance Criteria: Health, order, customer and summary endpoints return correct JSON, matching the database; unsupported methods return 405; unknown routes return 404.

Title: API input validation and paging
User Story: As an application developer, I want clear errors for bad input and working pagination, so that clients behave predictably.
Acceptance Criteria: limit must be 1-100 and offset >= 0, otherwise 400; pages do not overlap; non-numeric ids return 400.

Title: Dashboard data accuracy
User Story: As a business user, I want dashboard figures to match the source data, so that I can trust the insights.
Acceptance Criteria: Totals, counts and averages on the dashboard equal values calculated independently from the source.

Title: API performance
User Story: As an application developer, I want fast responses, so that the API is usable in applications.
Acceptance Criteria: Health, list and summary endpoints respond in under one second on the sample dataset.

Title: Dashboard filters and interaction
User Story: As a business user, I want filters, slicers and drill-downs to behave correctly, so that I can explore the data.
Acceptance Criteria: Each filter narrows the data correctly; clearing filters restores totals; drill-downs match underlying records.
